title: GitHub
description: Exposes GitHub repository operations as agent tools.
Covers files, issues, pull requests, reviews, releases, workflows, orgs, users,

github.authType.title: Authentication method
github.authType.description: Personal Access Token is simplest for individual/dev use. GitHub App auth mints short-lived, auto-rotating installation tokens — recommended for unattended pipelines against an org's repos.

github.token.title: Personal Access Token
github.token.description: GitHub PAT with repo, issues, pull_requests, and workflows scopes. Use a fine-grained token scoped to only the repos you need.

github.appId.title: App ID
github.appId.description: The numeric App ID from your GitHub App's settings page.

github.privateKey.title: App Private Key (.pem)
github.privateKey.description: Upload the PEM private key generated for your GitHub App. Used to sign short-lived JWTs; never sent to GitHub directly.

github.installationId.title: Installation ID
github.installationId.description: The installation ID for the org/account where the App is installed (found in the installation's settings URL).

github.defaultRepo.title: Default Repository
github.defaultRepo.description: Default repo in owner/repo format (e.g. acme/myapp). Tool calls that omit the repo parameter will use this value.

github.readOnly.title: Read-only mode
github.readOnly.description: When enabled, all write operations (file create/edit/delete, issue create, PR create, etc.) are blocked. Safe for agents that should only read.

github.tools.title: Tools
github.tools.description: Tool names to register, for example graphql, repo_tree, label_list. Only these appear in the schema the agent sees and only these can be called. Leave empty to register every tool. An unknown name stops the pipeline at start with the list of valid names.

github.graphqlAllowMutations.title: GraphQL mutations
github.graphqlAllowMutations.description: With read-only mode off, lets graphql run a document that contains a mutation operation. Off by default: a mutation can do anything the credential allows, such as merging a pull request, deleting a branch or changing branch protection, far more than the write tools. Read-only mode refuses mutations whatever this says.

github.graphqlMaxResponseBytes.title: GraphQL response cap (bytes)
github.graphqlMaxResponseBytes.description: Largest graphql response body the node reads, in bytes after decompression. A larger response returns an error naming this cap instead of the data. Default 4194304 (4 MiB).

github.rateLimitBudgetSeconds.title: Rate-limit wait budget (seconds)
github.rateLimitBudgetSeconds.description: Total time one call of graphql or a repository read (repo_tree, repo_contributors, repo_languages, label_list, user_get) may spend waiting out GitHub rate limits, across every request it makes: a repo_tree walk shares it among its subtree reads. A wait that does not fit is not started, and the call returns the rate-limit error with retry_after. When GitHub names no wait the waits are 60, 120, then 240 seconds, so the default allows one such retry; raise it to allow more. 0 never retries after a rate limit.

github.rateLimitMaxRetries.title: Rate-limit retries
github.rateLimitMaxRetries.description: Retries of each request after its first attempt when GitHub answers it with a rate limit, within the call's wait budget: 3 retries means up to 4 attempts. 0 never retries.
